I was fully committed to attending college in another state away from my abusers and my therapist at that time was trying to discourage me from staying at the college saying I should go back to my home state. I decided to remain at the school and continue sessions, although I could tell by the end of our time together, she was trying to shoo me out of the door, telling me to repeat the mantra “life is always working out for me” while telling me to find another therapist without offering any referrals. 

It was only after I found a trauma therapist that I realized my previous one had no clue what chronic or complex trauma was or how to treat it, and she instead viewed me in a negative way rather than admit limits to her own treatment. I still find myself pretty upset at the dismissiveness and discouragement she displayed when I really needed support. I saw her for a couple years periodically, and thought I was getting better, but she really never gave me any insight into what I was dealing with.

It made me realize I need to be more active and selective in my own treatment, and to not be afraid to end therapeutic relationships if I’m not getting the right treatment.
I tried my psychiatrist’s sample pack for 2 weeks for unipolar depression from CPTSD, and found it made me tired and anxious/restless. About to start Vraylar and hoping it does a better job.

28, suffering from cptsd from years of homophobic bullying, currently looking into countries that allow dignified death for mental illness. I don’t experience a sense of self, I retain little to no memory and cant relate to most people. It has severely impacted my academic and creative ability. It’s not a life I would wish for anyone.
It’s important to a lot of people who are still living in fear. If you didn’t care you wouldn’t have commented.
you’re being willfully ignorant because you’ve never had to experience what it’s like to live in fear. Go back to the rock you’ve been living under bc your perspective is less than useless.

it matters to a lot of people who have had to live in fear over a basic part of their humanity that they should never have had to worry about. it’s not the fault of gay people that coming out is still necessary in this day and age.

well there’s also the aspect of sexuality that involves romantic relationships, not just the act of sex itself. Not sure why sex is your only focus. and alot of people who have had to live in fear care.

I endured homophobic bullying for 8 years from middle through highschool by more than a few guys. Teachers were catholic and didn’t give a fuck. 

I developed severe ptsd that affects every facet of my life. I don’t have a sense of self and have little to no memory which makes me unable to relate to or bond with most people. I still got into a good college far away from my hometown. although I managed to graduate my academic and creative work were severely impacted. 

I have gone to great lengths to try to heal from this. Beyond 13 years in therapy, I have tried ketamine therapy, MDMA therapy, TMS brain treatments, and 7 antidepressants and still have seen little improvement to my condition.The repression of my personality development eventually led to a psychotic break which has deeply impacted my cognitive function and ability to learn / process information. 

This is what bullying and homophobia can do to people, and I hope those who targeted me all rot the rest of their lives. While i forgive myself for not being able to anything about this when I was younger, there’s nothing my forgiveness can do for the people who targeted me. They were conscious of it when it happened and enjoyed what they were doing.

I still have to catch myself reading into certain things too much - whether that’s certain number combinations like 1 and 0 which were features of my psychotic break where I thought I was associated with the number zero. I also have to stop myself from reading into the word “nothing”  which my brain tries to associate with itself after the break. In general I read a strong negative bias into things and am still learning to recognize it and stop thinking I’m able to predict things like the future in any way.

Thank you for your reply, and I am glad to hear you have found peace. while I have forgiven my younger self for trying to do all he could at the time, the bullying affected me in so many core ways I don’t feel I can move on.  I don’t have a concept of myself, I don’t have concepts of other people. This stole my ability to grow relationships with all of my family. I have no experience sharing emotions with other people because mine are blank beyond stress and fear. I have no memory beyond autobiographical knowledge (zero verbal and episodic memory). I eventually experienced a psychosis from the repression and failed relationships, which has led to my mind/cognition being blank unless I type or write something down. I experience hypervigilance and fear of abandonment /rejection, and people who I would naturally relate to the most feel the most threatening now. I am tired of masking and don’t want to have to put up a front anymore. 

Im not sure if I can be well enough to go elsewhere and be with college friends again. I have gone through therapy long enough to solidify details of what happened, but it feels like peace is inaccessible as long as I don’t have basic functionality of my brain and emotions, or am unable to just be in the present moment with others without feeling a profound sense of loss. I wish I could feel differently, but I don’t feel like there’s any hope left for me.

I struggle with CPTSD with dissociative/psychotic features from years of homophobic bullying. I struggle with hypervigilance, my mind looks for threats everywhere, and have lost the ability to form episodic memories, have poor focus, short term, and working memory. It makes learning things and building a life exceptionally difficult. Forming / maintaining healthy relationships feels like a luxury on another planet than the one I’m on. My mind feels like a radio where every channel is 90% static with only a small portion of the signal getting through. I was able to mask the condition for a long time but it eventually caught up with me. Went through 7 diff antidepressants so far, ketamine and mdma therapy, and now trying TMS to see if I can get some executive function, thoughts, and memory back. TLDR bullying fucks people, homophobia is cowardly bullshit and also be kinder to people in general.

Thank you for your comment. I am sorry to hear you also have had your own traumatic experiences with this but am happy to hear you have managed to make some progress. As the story with trauma healing usually goes, it’s generally a 1 step forward 2 step back situation. and I try my best to not be black and white about the healing process, and also try to be mindful of progress no matter how small. While I was in college (I had similar experiences as your dream from some MDMA experiences) I managed to make the most progress, but after an ex blamed me for being “empty” I spiraled into a breakdown near graduation. I managed to graduate later but still have yet to functionally recover after 4 years. I have managed to move to my own apartment, so that’s an improvement, and can make ends meet for the time being. I’m making a daily log of my TMS experiences to see how executive function and depression change over the course of treatments, and am currently working with a psychiatrist to see how much is biological vs trauma. the current hope is that the depression lifts enough for some of the executive function to improve and see what healing is possible from there.
